explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates CTRLEval (LLM-based metric) against human judgments on the same set of generated texts, reporting Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlations for each evaluation aspect

prompts.notes: Figure 1 shows example pattern designs for text infilling tasks. Main text describes pattern functions f and g for creating input/output sequences, including examples like 'The book is about NLP. [M] It depicts fancy models.'

guidelines.notes: Annotators rated on 1-5 Likert scale for each aspect. Quality control: submissions discarded if annotator assigned higher rating to negative sample than other texts. Negative samples constructed by perturbing (sentence shuffling/dropping) existing samples.

sample_size.validated_by_both: Same evaluation set for both LLM and human
sample_size.notes: Evaluation set includes sentiment-controlled (15 prefixes × 2 labels × 3 samples × 4 models = 360 texts) and topic-controlled (20 prefixes × 4 labels × 3 samples × 4 models = 960 texts) generations, plus negative samples

validation_results.summary_finding: CTRLEval consistently outperforms baseline metrics with Pearson correlations ranging from 0.2403-0.5189 across different aspects, showing better alignment with human judgments than alternative reference-free metrics.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-based CTRLEval and human evaluation assess the same three criteria: Coherence, Consistency, and Attribute Relevance, using identical evaluation aspects and the same set of generated texts.
